title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-2 World-Action Model
summary: Dyna Robotics announced DYNA-2 on August 10, 2026, a World-Action Model (WAM) it says is the first robot foundation model pretrained on more than 1 million hours of egocentric human video, roughly 170 years of continuous experience, with no robot teleoperation data used in pretraining. The company reports DYNA-2 completed 1.55x more tasks than its prior VLA-based model DYNA-1 in real customer deployments (87% vs. 46% pass rate) and improved instruction-following by 133% through a video co-training algorithm. In high-precision manufacturing tests, task success rose from 20% to 80-90% purely from pretraining scale, and a pair of five-fingered hands learned to twist open a bottle cap from 13 minutes of local fine-tuning data. Dyna frames the results as evidence of a scaling law driven by human video rather than scarce robot data, with a stated roadmap toward 10 million hours of training footage.
whyItMatters: If the claimed scaling law holds up to independent scrutiny, training generalist robot policies primarily on abundant human video rather than costly teleoperated robot data would remove one of the biggest bottlenecks to commercial robot deployment and ease cross-embodiment transfer between arms, humanoids and dexterous hands.
